summary: The Fagerstrom test for nicotine dependence calculator is a free, no-sign-up health tool. Fill in the 7 fields it asks for and it works out total score straight away, with the formula shown underneath. That makes it useful for an informed starting point to take to a clinician, not a diagnosis. Nothing is submitted anywhere: the arithmetic runs in the page you are looking at.

sections.title: How does the Fagerstrom test for nicotine dependence calculator work?
sections.html:
The Fagerstrom test for nicotine dependence calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports total score in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (which cigarette would you hate most to give up?).

Press Calculate and the page works through the equation with the values you supplied and derives the rest; it then keeps up with you as you correct a typo.

sections.title: What do you need to enter?
sections.html:
What you supply, field by field

7 fields on this form are a choice rather than a number. Those choices decide which version of the calculation applies, so they are worth setting before you worry about the digits.

sections.title: The formula behind the Fagerstrom test for nicotine dependence calculator
sections.html:
One relationship drives the whole page:

Total score=(how soon after you wake up do you smoke your first cigarette? + do you find it difficult to refrain from smoking in places where it is forbidden (e.g., in church, at the library, in the cinema)? + which cigarette would you hate most to give up? + how many cigarettes per day do you smoke? + do you smoke more frequently during the first hours after waking than during the rest of the day? + do you smoke when you are so ill that you are in bed most of the day?)

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:
• A number, filled in as soon as the inputs allow it.

If a number looks wrong, check three things in this order: that the units match what you had in mind, that no drop-down is still on its default, and that the value you entered is on the same scale as the rest — a rate typed as 5 rather than 0.05 is the classic mistake. Those three account for almost every answer that is out by a factor.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Fagerstrom test for nicotine dependence calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Tracking a measurement over time and understanding what changed
  • Preparing for an appointment so you can describe your numbers clearly
  • Deciding whether a reading is worth a second look

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Keep the units you enter consistent. Mixing centimetres into a field that expects metres is the single most common way to get an answer that is out by a factor of a hundred.
  • Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.
  • Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.
  • Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.

sections.title: What are the limits worth knowing?
sections.html:
Every tool draws a boundary somewhere. For the Fagerstrom test for nicotine dependence calculator, these are the ones that matter:

  • The 7 drop-downs on this page offer a fixed list of cases. A value that is not on the list cannot be entered, and the nearest option is not always a good substitute.
  • The calculator reports what the relationship implies; it does not judge whether the inputs themselves are sensible, so a figure that is out by a factor of ten will produce an answer that is out by the same factor.

faq.q: What does the Fagerstrom test for nicotine dependence calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns total score. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Fagerstrom test for nicotine dependence calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for a few values, which is 7 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There are several choices to make (7 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports Total score = 0. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the Fagerstrom test for nicotine dependence calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — press Calculate and every result updates together.
